title: Your First Class
goal: By the end of this lesson you will know how to write a tiny class using class and pass.
learn: Start a class with class Name:
Use pass for an empty body
Class names usually start with a capital letter
idea: You write a class like this: class Dog: pass pass means empty for now. Class names usually use CapWords like Dog or Player. The next lessons fill the class with attributes and methods.
changeOneLine: In the editor above, add print("Classes are blueprints") at the end and press Run.

practice.text: Define an empty class Cat with pass. Print a ready message.
practice.hint: After class Cat:, indent four spaces and write pass. The class body cannot be empty without pass.
practice.starterTip: Replace the blank line under class Cat: with pass (indented), then keep print("Cat ready") at the bottom.
practice.gradingNote: Pass if class Cat with pass exists and message prints.

practice.text: Define empty classes Car and Bike. Print two ready lines.
practice.hint: Write class Car: and class Bike:, each with an indented pass. Then two print() calls, one message per class.
practice.starterTip: Write class Car: with pass under it, then class Bike: with pass, then print("Car ready") and print("Bike ready").
practice.gradingNote: Pass if Car and Bike classes exist with pass.

quiz.question: Which starts a class?
quiz.correct: Right, you use the class keyword.

quiz.question: What does pass mean here?
quiz.correct: Yes, pass is a placeholder that fills the indented block.
quiz.wrong: It just means empty for now.

quiz.question: Usual style for class names?
quiz.correct: Right, CapWords is the usual style.

project.title: Name Three Classes
project.desc: Define three empty classes (using pass) for a tiny game world. Print a ready line for each.
project.starter:
class Hero:
